summary: The candidate is a meaningful partial hot-reload implementation, but its class-content copying breaks existing instances when a reloaded method uses zero-argument super(). Its own focused tests pass, yet an independent contract-level adversarial case fails deterministically, so it does not safely deliver the claimed general pure-Python class reload.

tests.what_was_measured: At the recorded base, neither the CLI flag nor the reload implementation exists, reproducing the original absence of a hot-reload path. Each check returned 1.
The candidate's five unit/regression cases pass at the exact candidate commit.

An existing subclass instance works before reload but fails afterward with TypeError when its reloaded method uses zero-argument super(); this directly tests the claimed existing-instance rebinding contract.
No native source files changed, so native rebuilding was not applicable.

gpu_execution_evidence: No GPU workload was run during this independent review. Hardware inventory found one AMD Instinct MI355X with gfx950. The decisive failure is a deterministic Python object-model error independent of GPU execution.
remaining_counterexamples: Reload a loaded pure-Python sglang.* module containing an inherited class whose updated method uses zero-argument super(), then call that method on an instance created before reload: the candidate raises TypeError because the copied function's __class__ closure refers to the new class while the instance belongs to the preserved old class.
remaining_limitations: Existing-instance rebinding is unsafe for ordinary zero-argument super() methods and therefore cannot support arbitrary selected pure-Python SGLang modules as documented.
Reload is non-transactional; a failure can leave workers or modules partially mutated.
Multi-rank synchronization and consistency after mixed worker success/failure were not hardware-tested.
Native extensions, newly imported modules, object-layout changes, process-topology changes, torch.compile artifacts, and JIT kernels remain unsupported.
The issue's alternative fault-tolerant scheduler event-loop behavior is not implemented.
No independent large-model weight-preservation timing, distributed workload, other model architecture, or GPU numerical validation was performed in this review.
